purpose: Download and checksum-verify the official upstream Dagu v2.17.0 linux_amd64 release, install it to a NEW isolated prefix (never replacing the pinned 2.16.6 install), and run the SAME accepted checkpoint/stop/retry job-recovery fixture (blueprints/convergence-practice/job-recovery/fixture.py, imported unmodified) against both the 2.16.6 pin and the freshly installed 2.17.0 binary, diffing the resulting checkpoint sha256 and stop/retry status transitions to see whether upstream latest changes in-flight/checkpoint-reuse behaviour relative to the pinned version.
preregistered: Formed before running: if 2.17.0 is a compatible minor/patch release with no breaking change to the stop/retry/checkpoint-reuse contract, the run should reach the same terminal states as the accepted 2.16.6 record (aborted -> succeeded, same dag-run id across the retry, and an IDENTICAL checkpoint.json sha256 to the previously accepted '59cb2038939b9cd2840eeaed6618634cad75ffe0f9a3b689a44f420f7847a1d0', since checkpoint.json's content is generated by our own fixture.py and does not depend on dagu internals). A settle-in-favor-of-2.17.0 result is: identical status transitions and identical checkpoint hash on both versions. A result that would change the verdict is: any exit-code failure, a different post-retry status, a different dag-run id linkage, or -- more importantly -- any difference in whether the interrupted finalizer process is actually terminated by `stop` (observed_owned_processes_remaining), which would indicate a real behavioural regression/improvement in crash-recovery semantics between versions.

commands.cmd: curl -fsSL -o checksums.txt https://github.com/dagucloud/dagu/releases/download/v2.17.0/checksums.txt && curl -fsSL -o dagu_2.17.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz https://github.com/dagucloud/dagu/releases/download/v2.17.0/dagu_2.17.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz && sha256sum dagu_2.17.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz && grep linux_amd64 checksums.txt
commands.output_excerpt: e9d4ac3c92f753439b40fc687e860acae4384d9692fb732e1285516811751e0d  dagu_2.17.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz (both the computed sha256sum and the value in the release's own checksums.txt match exactly)

commands.cmd: mkdir -p <local-tool-prefix>/dagu-2.17.0 && tar xzf dagu_2.17.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz -C <local-tool-prefix>/dagu-2.17.0 && chmod +x .../dagu && dagu version

status=passed dagu_version=2.17.0 before_retry_status=aborted after_retry_status=succeeded same_native_run_id=true checkpoint_sha256_unchanged=59cb2038939b9cd2840eeaed6618634cad75ffe0f9a3b689a44f420f7847a1d0 observed_owned_processes_remaining=0 command_exit_codes.all=0

result: Upstream Dagu v2.17.0 was downloaded, its tarball sha256 matched the release's own checksums.txt exactly, and it was installed to a brand-new prefix without touching the pinned 2.16.6 install. Running the identical, unmodified checkpoint/stop/retry fixture (via a version-parameterized wrapper of the accepted job-recovery/run.py, reusing job-recovery/fixture.py unchanged) against both binaries produced IDENTICAL outcomes: same status transitions (aborted -> succeeded), same dag-run-id linkage across the retry, same owned-process retirement (0 remaining after stop), all 7 native commands exit 0 on both versions, and -- critically -- the exact same checkpoint.json sha256 (59cb2038939b9cd2840eeaed6618634cad75ffe0f9a3b689a44f420f7847a1d0) as the previously accepted 2.16.6 record in job-recovery/README.md. No behavioural difference was observed for this fixture between 2.16.6 and 2.17.0.

verdict_impact.explanation: This closes the 'no result recorded for 2.17.0' gap with a genuine native-execution data point: the pinned 2.16.6 behaviour is reproduced exactly on the newer upstream release for the checkpoint/stop/retry contract that was already accepted, so there is no regression motivating an upgrade or a downgrade of confidence in the pin. It does not, by itself, motivate re-pinning to 2.17.0 (that would be a separate adoption decision outside this check's scope), and it does not test the in-flight-SIGKILL scenario covered by the separate dagu-inflight-resume-after-kill check, which was NOT re-run against 2.17.0 in this pass (out of this check's preregistered scope).

limitations: Only the graceful stop/retry/checkpoint-reuse fixture was diffed across versions; the SIGKILL/stale-lock finding from the companion dagu-inflight-resume-after-kill check was not separately re-run against 2.17.0, so parity on THAT specific failure mode between versions is unverified.
Single run per version, single host (WSL2 x86_64); not repeated for statistical confidence.

The fixture's checkpoint content is generated entirely by our own fixture.py (planner.py/test_planner.py oracle), so an identical checkpoint hash mainly demonstrates dagu's step-execution/env-passing contract is unchanged, not full parity across dagu's entire feature surface (e.g. queueing, coordinator/distributed mode, scheduler cron parsing were not exercised here).
